evidence.quote: This hardwood forest byway found in the Kinzua Bridge State Park in northwestern Pennsylvania has a skywalk that was constructed on six of the historic Kinzua Viaduct massive steel towers remaining after the tornado of 2003.

evidence.claim: The Kinzua Bridge Byway follows Route 3011 from Route 6 to Kinzua Bridge in McKean County.

evidence.claim: Its destination began as an iron railroad bridge in 1882, then was rebuilt in steel in 1900 to carry heavier trains.
evidence.quote: the wrought iron original 1882 structure held the record for the tallest railroad bridge in the world for two years. In 1900, the bridge was dismantled and simultaneously rebuilt out of steel to allow it to accommodate heavier trains.

evidence.claim: The original crossing carried a branch line toward Elk County’s coalfields, avoiding eight extra miles of track over rough terrain.
evidence.quote: building a branch line off the main line in Pennsylvania, from Bradford south to the coalfields in Elk County. The fastest way to do so was to build a bridge across the Kinzua Valley. The only other alternative would have been to lay an additional 8 miles (13 km) of track over rough terrain.

evidence.claim: Commercial service ended in 1959; Pennsylvania purchased the bridge in 1963 as the centerpiece of a state park.
evidence.quote: It stayed in commercial service until 1959, when it was sold to a salvage company. In 1963 the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania purchased the bridge as the centerpiece of a state park.

evidence.claim: In July 2003, a tornado brought down eleven of its twenty spans.
evidence.quote: At approximately 3:20 p.m., July 21, 2003, a tornado from the east touched down at the park. The storm, classified as F-1 on the Fujita scale, tore down 11 of the 20 structure spans

evidence.claim: The fallen sections were left where they landed, making the wreckage part of the park’s landscape.
evidence.quote: They have been left as they fell

evidence.claim: Badly rusted bolts at the tower bases caused the failure; sections fell intact before striking the ground.
evidence.quote: The failure was caused by badly rusted bolts holding the bases of the towers. The investigation reckoned that the whole structure oscillated laterally 4-5 times before fatigue broke the base bolts. The towers fell intact in sections, and they suffered impact damage with the ground.

evidence.claim: Six surviving steel towers support the Sky Walk.
evidence.quote: a skywalk that was constructed on six of the historic Kinzua Viaduct massive steel towers remaining after the tornado of 2003.

evidence.claim: Opened on September 15, 2011, the walkway ends at an observation deck with glass flooring that reveals the bridge and valley below.
evidence.quote: The Kinzua Sky Walk was opened on September 15, 2011, in a ribbon-cutting ceremony. The Sky Walk consists of a pedestrian walkway to an observation deck with a glass floor at the end of the bridge that allows views of the bridge and the valley directly below.

evidence.claim: The steel belongs to the bridge rebuilt in 1900 for heavier trains, replacing the original wrought-iron structure.
evidence.quote: In 1900, the bridge was dismantled and simultaneously rebuilt out of steel to allow it to accommodate heavier trains.

evidence.claim: Even after that rebuilding, trains were limited to five miles per hour.
evidence.quote: Even after being reconstructed, the bridge still had a speed limit of 5 miles per hour (8 km/h).

evidence.claim: The pedestrian walkway extends 600 feet along the remaining supports.
evidence.quote: visitors can stroll 600 feet out on the remaining support towers

evidence.claim: The reconstruction reused the original anchor bolts, a decision that later contributed to the bridge’s collapse when corrosion weakened those connections.
evidence.quote: The bolts used to hold the towers to the anchor blocks were reused from the first bridge, which would eventually play a major role in the bridge's demise.

evidence.claim: The reconstruction reused the original anchor bolts, a decision that later contributed to the bridge’s collapse when corrosion weakened those connections.
